text:
Maya: Heads-up — saw a weird client/server timing delta in streaming for /v1/generate after yesterday's kernel selection tweak. Client traces show inconsistent chunk cadence. anyone else?
Jon: I noticed on my smoke tests too. Server emit intervals steady ~40ms but client receives bursts then gaps (30-120ms).
Sam: can you paste a brief trace or logs?
Maya: quick svclog from a repro run: ```
# client chunk receives (ms since start)
0, 38, 76, 210, 246, 284, 380, 420
# server chunk emits (ms since start)
0, 40, 80, 120, 160, 200, 240, 280
```
Sam: that looks like client-side pacing/backpressure. but weird it's so periodic on server. did the kernel selection change add micro-batching?
Maya: yes, last night we changed kernel heuristic to prefer compact kernels for short sequences — could affect batch formation.
Arya: I profiled the runtime on a repro node. KV miss spikes align with the client gaps. when kv_miss_rate > ~15% we see a 60-120ms tail added to some chunks (fallback kernel path).
Lucas: can you share the profiling snippet?
Arya: ```
# simplified flame samples (ms)
serve_emit: 40
kernel_dispatch: 10
kv_lookup: 8
kv_miss_recovery: 90  # correlated with gaps
network_send: 2
```
Jon: hypothesis: compact kernels + higher KV miss -> some requests take fallback path that delays the next emit window and the client-side pacing queues then emits in a burst.
Maya: repro steps I used: ```
# run local repro
./bin/run_inference --model t5-xxl --route /v1/generate --clients 8 --client-pacing auto --seq 128 --kv-populate 30%
# collect tracing
curl -s localhost:8080/trace?run=1 > trace.json
```
Sam: short-term mitigation: pin route to older kernel using rollout override `{ "kernel_hint": "legacy_compact_v2" }` or force `--max_batch_size=64`. that reduces the miss-induced jitter in my tests.
Maya: created a dashboard card to visualize per-route chunk gaps + kv_miss_rate. query suggestion: `sum(rate(stream_chunk_received_count[1m])) by (route)` and for per-token latency: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`.
Lucas: I'll add a Grafana panel and an alert: if p95_chunk_interval(route) > 100ms and kv_miss_rate(route) > 0.1 then fire. example promql for p95 chunk interval: `quantile_over_time(0.95, increase(stream_chunk_emit_time_seconds_sum[5m]) / increase(stream_chunk_emit_time_seconds_count[5m])) by (route)` — might need adjustments.
Arya: also recommending adding an exported label on each chunk event: `server_ts` and `chunk_seq` so client/server diffs are easier to compute in dashboards.
Sam: small runtime patch idea: when kv_miss detected, do not immediately switch to fallback kernel mid-batch; instead finish current emit window then switch. reduces interleaving jitter.
Maya: filing an RFC issue: https://redwoodinc.internal/r/infra/stream-chunk-cadence — added repro logs and perf runs.
infra-bot: test job queued (job id: 72514) for canary with `--max_batch_size=64` on /v1/generate.
Lucas: I'll own the dashboard + alert; Arya can prototype the kernel gating change; Sam you ok to run the canary and collect traces?
Sam: yes, running now — will paste results in this thread in ~10m. :hourglass:
